function.mechanism: Provides sweetness with partial intestinal absorption; unabsorbed fraction is fermented/osmotically active in the gut, which can cause laxative effects at high intake.

adi.basis: SCF allocation referenced by EFSA: ADI not specified for maltitol and maltitol syrup.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA 2006 found no safety concern for the proposed amendment of maltitol syrup specifications; EFSA 2023 call states available data were insufficient to assess potential genotoxicity in re-evaluation context and requested new data.

concerns.summary: Dose-related gastrointestinal intolerance (osmotic diarrhea) is the most consistent human adverse effect at higher bolus intakes.
Older in vitro data reported weak genotoxic potential signals, while EFSA's current re-evaluation workflow identifies insufficient data to fully resolve potential genotoxicity concerns.
High-dose rat developmental study reported reduced fetal weight/growth retardation at the highest tested dose despite no teratogenic classification in that study.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2006 opinion concluded no safety concern for proposed maltitol syrup specification amendment.
JECFA lists ADI as not limited for maltitol.
FDA CFR 21 CFR 184.1924 affirms maltitol syrup as generally recognized as safe when used under GMP conditions.

populations: high consumers of sugar-free polyol products
adi_exceedance.notes: Regulatory ADIs are non-numeric (not specified/not limited), so numeric ADI exceedance is not directly computed; practical risk is mainly high-intake GI intolerance.

risk_assessment.rationale: Maltitol is broadly authorized (EU/FDA/JECFA) with no major carcinogenic classification identified, and the main well-established adverse effect is high-dose gastrointestinal intolerance. EFSA's ongoing data call on genotoxicity uncertainty supports caution but does not currently justify a higher-risk tier.
key_factors: EFSA 2006 no-safety-concern conclusion for specification amendment
EFSA 2023 call noting insufficient genotoxicity-relevant data for re-evaluation
FDA GRAS affirmation in 21 CFR 184.1924 under GMP
Human evidence of osmotic diarrhea at higher bolus doses
